descriptionChirho: Intransitive Qal sense of departing into captivity or exile, including substantive participle uses meaning 'exile, one in exile' (Arabic cognate: جلا jalaa / سُبي subiya).
Transitive Qal sense of revealing, disclosing, or making known information, secrets, or divine matters (Arabic cognate: كشف kashafa; Korean: 드러내다; Swahili: kufunua).
Intransitive Qal sense of departing, vanishing, or being carried away, distinct from exile proper (Arabic cognates: ارتحل irtahala, ذهب dhahaba, يزول yazulu; Korean: 떠나다).
Stative/adjectival use of the Qal passive participle indicating a state of being open, uncovered, or exposed (Arabic: مكشوف makshuf; Korean: 열린/드러난; Swahili: wazi).

Nifal (and Pual) reflexive-passive sense of being revealed, being uncovered, appearing, or manifesting oneself, including divine self-revelation (Arabic: انكشف inkashafa / أُعلن u'lina; Korean: 드러나다/나타나다).
Piel factitive sense of physically uncovering, stripping bare, removing a covering, or exposing nakedness (Arabic: كشف kashafa physical; Korean: 벗기다; Hindi: उघाड़ना).

Piel factitive sense of revealing information, disclosing secrets, or making divine truths known, extending the uncovering metaphor to abstract domains (Arabic: كشف kashafa abstract; Korean: 드러내다; Hindi: प्रकट करना).
Hitpael reflexive sense of uncovering or exposing oneself, often with connotations of shameful self-exposure (Arabic: انكشف reflexive; Korean: 벗겨졌다).
Hifil causative sense of causing someone to go into exile, deporting, or carrying away captive (Arabic: سبى sabaa / أجلى ajlaa; Korean: 사로잡아 갔다/추방했다; Swahili: kupeleka uhamishoni).
Hofal passive of the Hifil, indicating being exiled, deported, or carried into captivity by an external agent (Arabic: جُلي juliya / سُبي subiya passive; Korean: 잡혀갔다/유배당한).
